full_judgment:
A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J:- This petition for leave to appeal by the defendant is from the judgment and order dated 15.6.1998 of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 3859 of 1995, making the Rule absolute and the sending the case back to the trial Court for disposal. 

 4. The trial Court dismissed the suit ex parte with the findings that the plaintiff could not prove his case and there was no evidence adduced by him to prove that defendant attained majority on 2.3.84 as claimed by the plaintiff. The lower appellate Court decreed the suit and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Against the judgment and decree of the lower Appellate Court passed on 26.6.95 in -0. C. Appeal No. 29 of 1994 reversing those of the trial Court dated 13.11.93 made in 0. C. Suit No. 11 of 1987, the defendant-petitioner Sree Amal Bhushan Singha obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3859 of 1995. The Rule was made absolute setting aside the judgment and decree of the courts below and sending the suit on remand to the trial Court for disposal in accordance with law. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the petitioner contends that in view of his own riding that the Bainapatra was not moved before the Court in accordance ?Jai law the learned Single Judge corn-mated error of law in not dismissing the suit and--in sending it on remand to the T al Court for disposal. It is also argued "at the learned Judge of the High Court Division committed grave error of law in not deciding the case himself and thus striking his responsibility though the entire record was before him. It is contended that the learned Judge of the High Court Division totally misconceived and misconstrued the principle of law in remanding a case to the trial Court. The Court Division failed to notice that the purpose of remand is not to give a party a chance to fill up the lacuna in his case particularly in a suit for specific performance of contract. Further submission of the learned Advocate was that the High Court Division fell into an error of law in not dismissing the suit in as much as the plaintiff failed to prove the alleged contract and passing of consideration money. On a reference to the judgment of the High Court Division it is seen that it held that the real question of controversy' has not been adjudicated on the basis of evidence. Upon such finding the High Court Division remanded the case the trial Court for the ends of justice and ordered that the par-ties should be given opportunity to prove their respective case in accordance with law. As the High Court Division remanded the case for fresh trial with liberty to the parties to adduce evidence to prove their cases the order of remand was made legally we do not find that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division occasioned any failure of justice. In that view of the matter, we do not find any sub-stance in any of the contentions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
